title: Test-Time Debiasing with Probabilistic Prompts via Wasserstein Distance in Vision-Language Models
claim: Point-based prior corrections ignore group distributions; ours builds reference distributions, learns probabilistic prompts, and aligns embeddings via Wasserstein distance at test time.
layout: Multi-panel: limitations inset top-left, data prepare bottom-left, Phase I top-right, Phase II bottom-right
description: A dense, color-coded pipeline diagram with four regions. A gray inset at top-left, titled "Limitations of prior methods", shows 2-D scatter ellipses and a point-based shift. Below it, a blue "Data Prepare" block holds inputs (labeled training set, test query), a frozen CLIP-like encoder, and a "Build Reference Distributions" box with group ellipses and the query distribution. A green "Phase I: Probabilistic Prompt Learning" panel takes up the top right. It trains a prompt distribution with a learnable φ. Three loss boxes (debias/Wasserstein, contrastive performance, orthogonal bias subspace) feed a combined loss L_all, with a debias target below. An orange "Phase II: Inference" strip at the bottom right samples prompts, adds them to the query embedding E_Q, and passes the result to downstream tasks and metrics. The eye goes first to the large green Phase I region.

abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) inherit social biases from large-scale pretraining data, and these biases can amplify in downstream tasks, leading to systematic performance disparities across sensitive groups. Due to the high training cost and the risk of catastrophic forgetting, recent research has focused more on lightweight \emph{test-time} debiasing, aiming to obtain an ideal fair embedding for each query. However, such point-based corrections are often unstable and become notably weaker in multi-class settings, where group structure cannot be adequately captured by a single point. Therefore, we propose W4D, a distributional debiasing framework that reframes fairness as aligning query embedding distributions to group reference distributions under the Wasserstein distance, which provides a geometry-aware notion of discrepancy beyond mean shifts. To make this alignment practical at test-time, W4D introduces probabilistic prompts that induce controlled distributional perturbations and optimizes a Wasserstein-based objective to reduce cross-group disparity while preserving task-relevant semantics. This distributional perspective improves robustness in multi-class debiasing and yields a stronger fairness--utility trade-off across diverse VLM downstream evaluations. Our code is available at https://github.com/QDRhhhh/W4D.
